chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Abu Habeeb, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to the woman while she is menstruating. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is obligatory upon him, at the beginning of the menstruation, one Dinar, and at its ending, half a Dinar.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, is something of the Hadd (fixed penalty) obligatory upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, twenty-five lashes, a quarter of the Hadd of the adulterer, because he engaged in unlawful intercourse.'

key_terms.الدِّينَارُ: A gold coin used as a unit of currency in legal fines

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a man having intercourse with a menstruating woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific financial and corporal penalties for marital intercourse during menstruation, distinguishing between the timing of the act relative to the flow. Scholarly tradition interprets the 'quarter of the adulterer's punishment' (25 lashes) as a distinct hadd for this specific act, while the dinar fines reflect the juristic calculation of diyah based on whether the act occurred during the active flow or the subsequent period. This highlights the Shia emphasis on precise legal categorization of marital relations and their corresponding penalties.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far, from Abu Habeeb, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the man who came to the woman and she was Fasting. Heasws said: ‘It would be Obligated upon him, during the beginning of the menstruation, one Dinar, and during its ending, half a Dinar’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! Is something from the Penalty (Hadd) Obligated upon him?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, twenty five lashes, being a quarter of the Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer, because he came unlawfully’.
